No. of gram equivalent of metal carbonate required to neutralize 200 ml of 0.1 HCl = 0.2*0.1 = 0.02 gram equivalents

i.e. 0.02 gram equivalent = 1 gm

i.e. 1 gram equivalent = 50 gm

Equivalent weight of metal carbonate = 50 gm

Equivalent Weight of carbonate ion = (12+16*3)/2 = 30 gm

Now, Equivalent weight of metal = Equivalent weight of metal carbonate - Equivalent weight of metal = 50 gm - 30 gm = 20 gm

data.question_title: 100ml of 0.4N-HCl is mixed with 100ml of 0.6N of \(\text{H\({}_{2}\)SO\({}_{4}\).}\) What is the normality of the resulting solution?
data.explanation_txt:
100 ml of 0.4N HCl = 40 ml of 1N HCl

100 ml of 0.6N \(H_2SO_4\) = 60 ml of 1N \(H_2SO_4\)

Equivalent addition = 100 ml of 1N acid

Since the total volume of solution after the addition of individual acids is 200 ml, so 100 ml of 1N acid = 200 ml of 0.5N acid.

Hence, the normality of the solution is 0.5N.
